raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

For hybrid Gated DeltaNet (GDN) models with the mamba radix cache, a request that reuses a cached prefix gets slightly different results than the same prompt computed without the cache. Under `--enable-deterministic-inference` this breaks the guarantee: whether a request hits the cache depends on scheduling and timing, so its log-probabilities change from run to run.

Cause: when a prefill crosses a radix-cache checkpoint, `GDNAttnBackend` asks the extend kernel for an fp32 snapshot of the recurrent state at that chunk boundary (`track_state` / `track_chunk_idx`). `TritonGDNKernel` does not declare `supports_track_state_snapshot`, so the backend falls back to the per-chunk states `h`, which `chunk_gated_delta_rule` stores in the activation dtype (bf16) - the fallback's docstring says so ("already rounded to the activation dtype"). A request resuming from that checkpoint starts from a rounded state; its prefill output can still match (the output kernel reads the same rounded `h`), but the state it then decodes from differs, so the first decode step changes.

The shared chunk kernel (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`) already writes the fp32 snapshot; KDA's Triton kernel uses it. Only the GDN path does not pass it through.

Measured on MI350X with Qwen3.8-27B, `test_deterministic --test-mode prefix --return-logprob` workload with each sample's `meta_info.cached_tokens` recorded (1,700+ samples per run): with `--max-running-requests 16`, every sample that hit a checkpoint (at 64, 384 or 768 tokens) differed from the reference at its first decode step, and every sample without a hit matched. At default settings few samples hit the cache, and the mismatches (14 and 24 samples in two runs) were all among them.

## Modifications

- `chunk_gated_delta_rule` (and its autograd function and `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd`): optional `track_state` / `track_chunk_idx`, passed to `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`.
- `TritonGDNKernel`: `supports_track_state_snapshot = True` where it uses that kernel (not on CPU, NPU or XPU, which have their own kernels), and `extend` passes the snapshot arguments through.
- `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`: new case `test_resume_from_track_snapshot_matches_full_prefill`: resuming the second chunk of a 128-token sequence from the fp32 snapshot gives bitwise the same output and final state as one prefill; resuming from the bf16 per-chunk state does not.
- `test_mamba_track_state_dtype.py` (CPU): new `TestTritonGDNTrackSnapshot`: `TritonGDNKernel` declares the snapshot capability, `extend` forwards `track_state` / `track_chunk_idx` to `chunk_gated_delta_rule`, and forwards nothing when the capability is off.
- No change to checkpoint positions or to requests without cache hits. This applies in all modes: cached-prefix results now match uncached ones.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.21-rocm724-mi35x-20261012` with this change applied, Qwen3.8-27B BF16, `--attention-backend triton --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton --linear-attn-decode-backend triton --enable-deterministic-inference` (with #43788, #34543, #44076 and #44194 also applied, so that only this effect remains).

Unit tests: `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py`: before, 1 failed, 30 passed; after, 31 passed. `test_mamba_track_state_dtype.py` (CPU): before, 2 of the 3 new wiring tests fail (6 passed); after, 8 passed.

Prefix workload with `cached_tokens` recorded, samples whose log-probabilities differ from the first sample of the same prompt:

| Setting | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--max-running-requests 16` | 694 of 1,285 samples differ: exactly the 694 cache hits | 0 of 1,285 and 0 of 1,300 (694 and 714 cache hits) |
| defaults | 14 of 1,285 and 24 of 1,300 differ, all cache hits (32 and 37 hits) | 0 and 0 (32 and 37 cache hits) |

(Prompts with the 511-, 2,048- and 4,097-token prefixes; the 1-token prefix never hits the cache.)

`python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (50 trials) and the bitwise check of 1,275 responses, default settings (overlap scheduler and radix cache on). These runs follow the existing deterministic end-to-end tests (`TestDeterministicBase`, e.g. `test_qwen35_deterministic.py`), which are CUDA-only and compare decoded text only; here log-probabilities and the bitwise check are compared as well. Happy to add an AMD end-to-end test if wanted.

- Before: the `prefix --return-logprob` log-probability comparison differed in 8 of 13 runs (TP1 and TP2, `SGLANG_USE_AITER` 0 and 1).
- After: TP1 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`, TP1 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` and TP2 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` pass every mode (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob` with identical log-probabilities, `radix_cache`) and the bitwise check (1275 / 1275).

`p_vs_d` (prefill vs decode) still differs, as it does for every model.

GSM8K (all 1,319 questions, temperature 0, `sgl-eval` 0.1.2), Qwen3.8-27B: 95.91% in normal mode (`--attention-backend aiter`, without these changes), 96.06% with `--enable-deterministic-inference` and this change together with #43788, #34543, #44076 and #44194.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The backend now allocates an fp32 snapshot buffer for extend batches with tracked rows (it already did for snapshot-capable kernels). Qwen3.8-27B TP1, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf --seed 1 --warmup-requests 8 --flush-cache`, median of 2 runs, before and after on the same GPU, both GPU orders:

| Mode, workload | GPU | before tok/s | after tok/s | ratio | ITL p50 | TTFT p50 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| deterministic (`SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), 1k/1k, 256 prompts, concurrency 256 | A | 1,373.3 | 1,372.7 | 1.000x | 56.38 / 56.46 ms | 72.4 / 72.6 s |
| | B | 1,384.7 | 1,384.9 | 1.000x | 56.12 / 56.13 ms | 71.7 / 71.7 s |
| normal (`--attention-backend aiter`), 1k/1k, 256 / 256 | C | 2,256.2 | 2,256.0 | 1.000x | 27.84 / 27.93 ms | 36.2 / 36.1 s |
| | D | 2,289.5 | 2,291.7 | 1.001x | 27.53 / 27.55 ms | 35.5 / 35.4 s |
| normal, 8k/1k, 256 prompts, concurrency 128 | E | 1,047.1 | 1,045.3 | 0.998x | 37.26 / 37.30 ms | 36.1 / 36.1 s |
| | F | 1,047.5 | 1,048.3 | 1.001x | 37.08 / 37.07 ms | 36.2 / 36.1 s |

No measurable change.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+    def test_resume_from_track_snapshot_matches_full_prefill(self):
+        """Resuming a prefill from the fp32 track snapshot must give bitwise the same
+        output and final state as one prefill over the whole sequence; resuming from the
+        per-chunk state h (rounded to bf16) does not, which made prefix-cache hits on
+        hybrid GDN models change their decode results."""
+        device = get_device()
+        Hk, Hv, K, V, L = 16, 48, 128, 128, 128
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        q = torch.randn(1, L, Hk, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        k = torch.randn(1, L, Hk, K, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        v = torch.randn(1, L, Hv, V, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        g = -torch.rand(1, L, Hv, dtype=torch.float32, device=device) * 0.5
+        beta = torch.rand(1, L, Hv, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=device)
+        idx = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+
+        def run(lo, state, **track):
+            cu_seqlens = torch.tensor([0, L - lo], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+            o, _, h = chunk_gated_delta_rule(
+                *(t[:, lo:] for t in (q, k, v, g, beta)),
+                initial_state=state,
+                initial_state_indices=idx,
+                cu_seqlens=cu_seqlens,
+                head_first=False,
+                use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+                **track,
+            )
+            return o, h
+
+        full_state = torch.zeros(1, Hv, V, K, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
+        snapshot = torch.empty_like(full_state)
+        o_full, h_full = run(
+            0,
+            full_state,
+            track_state=snapshot,
+            track_chunk_idx=torch.ones(1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device),
+        )
+        resumed_state = snapshot.clone()
+        o_resumed, _ = run(64, resumed_state)
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(o_resumed, o_full[:, 64:]))
+        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(resumed_state, full_state))
+
+        rounded_state = h_full[0, 1].float().unsqueeze(0).contiguous()
+        run(64, rounded_state)
+        self.assertFalse(torch.equal(rounded_state, full_state))
+
     def _check_shape(
         self, B, T_per_seq, H, K, V, pool_size, sequential_indices=False, seed=42
     ):

+class TestTritonGDNTrackSnapshot(CustomTestCase):
+    """The Triton GDN kernel hands the fp32 track snapshot to the chunk kernel.
+
+    Without the snapshot, prefix-cache checkpoints fall back to the per-chunk
+    states ``h``, which are rounded to the activation dtype. The CPU, NPU and
+    XPU paths use other chunk kernels and keep that fallback.
+    """
+
+    def _extend(self, kernel):
+        chunk = Mock(return_value=sentinel.output)
+        x = torch.zeros(1, 2, 1, 2)
+        with (
+            patch.object(gdn_triton, "chunk_gated_delta_rule", chunk),
+            patch.object(gdn_triton, "is_cpu", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(gdn_triton, "is_npu", return_value=False),
+        ):
+            output = kernel.extend(
+                x,
+                x,
+                x,
+                x[..., 0],
+                x[..., 0],
+                ssm_states=torch.zeros(4, 1, 2, 2),
+                cache_indices=torch.tensor([3]),
+                query_start_loc=torch.tensor([0, 2]),
+                track_state=sentinel.track_state,
+                track_chunk_idx=sentinel.track_chunk_idx,
+            )
+        self.assertIs(output, sentinel.output)
+        chunk.assert_called_once()
+        return chunk.call_args.kwargs
+
+    def test_gpu_kernel_supports_the_snapshot(self):
+        self.assertTrue(TritonGDNKernel.supports_track_state_snapshot)
+
+    def test_extend_passes_the_snapshot_to_the_chunk_kernel(self):
+        kwargs = self._extend(TritonGDNKernel())
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["track_state"], sentinel.track_state)
+        self.assertIs(kwargs["track_chunk_idx"], sentinel.track_chunk_idx)
+
+    def test_extend_without_snapshot_support_passes_nothing(self):
+        kernel = TritonGDNKernel()
+        kernel.supports_track_state_snapshot = False
+        kwargs = self._extend(kernel)
+        self.assertNotIn("track_state", kwargs)
+        self.assertNotIn("track_chunk_idx", kwargs)
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     unittest.main()
